note: DERIVED. Drafted on 2026-11-15 by an AI session under D34 of issue #77. Row 17 of HOJA_COTEJO_CARBONO_22.md. D197 of issue #77 (inputs computed as AMG computes them, so the model is used as it was calibrated). The id, scope key crop and unit are those engine/residues/_parameters.py reads on main (RECORDS, CROP_SCOPE_KEY); the scope value is the crop_id of the demonstration rotations (D128). Arithmetic (D197): root dry matter 0-20 cm = yield x DRY / (SR x HI) x (1 - Beta^20). Yield 2221.125 kg ha-1 (signed record rusle2_crop_yield.soybean, params/records/residues/); DRY 0.91; SR 7.517; HI 0.32; Beta 0.939. 2221.125 x 0.91 = 2021.224; 7.517 x 0.32 = 2.40544; 2021.224 / 2.40544 = 840.27; 1 - 0.939^20 = 0.71600; 840.27 x 0.71600 = 601.64, rounded to 601.6 kg ha-1 (DERIVED). The depth 20 cm is the soil depth of D180. Verbatim cells to compare: parameters_PLANT.tab "MC,Soybean,Soja,C3,0.267,0.567,0.101,0.066,0.939,0.32,7.517,0.4,0.276,0.4,0.44,0.4,Solebiom project" (SR 7.517, HI 0.32, Beta 0.939). IPCC Table 11.1A (New), row "Soybeans 0.008 (± 75%)d 0.008 (± 75%)d 2.1 0.19 (± 45%) 0.91", last column "Dry matter fraction of harvested product (DRY)" = 0.91 (read on the local copy research_notes/validador_ia/IPCC2019-ch11.pdf, MD5 06c11d4f5a2b729564f8b3bd1ba11824, PDF p. 18). Clivot et al. (2019), printed p. 102: eq. 8 C_R = Y_P / (SR x HI) x 0.40 and eq. 10, the cumulative belowground fraction BGF = 1 - Beta^Depth (Gale and Grigal 1987). Limits (D197): the dataset's shoot:root ratios carry a coefficient of variation near 50 % (Clivot et al. 2019, section 2.5.2); no root biomass was measured at La Estanzuela; the yield is a national mean read as dry matter (D196). The dataset description says: "They are applicable for average French arable crop conditions." D192 and D197 of issue #77 take them as French defaults, not calibrated for Uruguay, and say so in the label. Per D161 no AI session writes a person's name in checked_by: the lead developer, or their delegate (D66), fills it after comparing the text with the source.
